  "body": "# Telegram Bot API

> The Bot API is an HTTP-based interface created for developers keen on building bots for Telegram.  
> To learn how to create and set up a bot, please consult our [**Introduction to Bots**](https://core.telegram.org/bots) and [**Bot FAQ**](https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq).

### Recent changes

> Subscribe to [@BotNews](https://t.me/botnews) to be the first to know about the latest updates and join the discussion in [@BotTalk](https://t.me/bottalk)

#### November 9, 2026

**Bot API 10.4**

**Widgets**

* Added the class [Widget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widget) and the field *widget* to the classes [Message](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#message) and [ExternalReplyInfo](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#externalreplyinfo) for messages with [HTML widgets](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets).
* Added the method [sendWidget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendwidget), allowing bots to send messages with HTML widgets. Currently, in the production environment, widgets can be sent only to private chats, and sent widgets automatically have protected content and therefore can't be forwarded.
* Added the method [sendSharedWidget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendsharedwidget), allowing bots to send again shared widgets created by the bot.
* Added the class [WidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquery) and the field *widget\_query* to the class [Update](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update) for queries sent to the bot by widgets in messages sent by the bot or via the bot.
* Added the class [SharedWidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sharedwidgetquery) and the field *shared\_widget\_query* to the class [Update](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update) for queries sent to the bot from forwarded messages with shared widgets.
* Added the classes [WidgetQueryType](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquerytype), [WidgetQueryTypeData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquerytypedata), [WidgetQueryTypeSignData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquerytypesigndata), [WidgetQueryTypeSentTransaction](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquerytypesenttransaction) and [WidgetQueryWallet](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquerywallet), describing the type of a query from a widget. * Added the method [answerWidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#answerwidgetquery), allowing bots to answer queries from widgets.
* Added the method [editMessageWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editmessagewidgetdata), allowing bots to change data of a widget in a message.
* Added the method [editSharedWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editsharedwidgetdata), allowing bots to change public data of a shared widget.
* Added the classes [InputWidgetMessageContent](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#inputwidgetmessagecontent) and [InputSharedWidgetMessageContent](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#inputsharedwidgetmessagecontent), allowing bots to send widgets in response to inline queries. Currently, widgets can't be sent in response to inline queries in the production environment.
* Widget messages can't be copied using the methods [copyMessage](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#copymessage) and [copyMessages](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#copymessages).
* The right *can\_send\_other\_messages* in the classes [ChatPermissions](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#chatpermissions) and [ChatMemberRestricted](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#chatmemberrestricted) now also allows sending widgets.

* Allowed bots to send ephemeral replies to callback queries in any chat except channel direct messages chats by specifying *callback\_query\_id* without *receiver\_user\_id* in the parameter *ephemeral\_message\_parameters* of the methods [sendMessage](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendmessage), [sendRichMessage](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendrichmessage), [sendAnimation](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendanimation), [sendAudio](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendaudio), [sendContact](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendcontact), [sendDocument](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#senddocument), [sendLivePhoto](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendlivephoto), [sendLocation](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendlocation), [sendPhoto](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendphoto), [sendSticker](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendsticker), [sendVenue](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendvenue), [sendVideo](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendvideo), [sendVideoNote](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendvideonote) and [sendVoice](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendvoice).

* Added the classes [ChatShareThemeBackdrop](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#chatsharethemebackdrop) and [ChatShareThemeBackdrops](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#chatsharethemebackdrops) and the method [getChatShareThemeBackdrops](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getchatsharethemebackdrops).

**Gifts**

* Added the method [deleteBusinessAccountGift](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#deletebusinessaccountgift), allowing bots to delete regular gifts owned by a managed business account without receiving Telegram Stars for them.

* Added updates about user stopping message generation, represented by the class [MessageGenerationStopped](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#messagegenerationstopped) and the field *stopped\_message\_generation* in the class [Update](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update).
* Added the class [CommunityChatJoined](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#communitychatjoined) and the field *community\_chat\_joined* to the class [Message](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#message) for service messages about join of a chat from a community.
* Added the fields *text*, *entities* and *is\_private* to the class [UniqueGiftInfo](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#uniquegiftinfo).

* Added the class [InputRichBlockListItem](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#inputrichblocklistitem), which represents an item in a list to be sent.

* Added the method [deleteEphemeralMessage](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#deleteephemeralmessage) allowing bots to delete ephemeral messages.

**Communities**

* Introduced initial support for **Communities** - several supergroups, channels, and bots linked together around a shared topic or audience.
* Added the class [Community](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#community) which represents a community.

### Authorizing your bot

Each bot is given a unique authentication token [when it is created](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#botfather). The token looks something like `123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11`, but we'll use simply **<token>** in this document instead. You can learn about obtaining tokens and generating new ones in [this document](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#botfather).

### Making requests

All queries to the Telegram Bot API must be served over HTTPS and need to be presented in this form: `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME`. Like this for example:

```
https://api.telegram.org/bot123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11/getMe
```

The format is the same everywhere (sending, inline results, changes):

* The chat state and the shared state are each a text of up to **1024 bytes** (bytes of UTF-8, not characters: 512 Cyrillic letters fill it), often JSON. The server does not interpret it.
* At sending, a field not passed means no state. In a change, a field not passed stays as it is, and an empty text clears it. The widget never sees an empty text: a cleared or absent state is `null`.

When the bot changes the state, a running widget gets `chatDataChanged` or `publicDataChanged` with the new state already in place (for a shared widget's shared state, only if the widget called `watchPublicData()`). Nothing restarts and the page keeps what it has drawn, so redraw from the state. A change that touches both fires both, `chatDataChanged` first. A change that leaves one of them as it was fires nothing for it.

const W = window.TelegramWidget;
function render() {
  let game = null;
  try { game = JSON.parse(W.chatData); } catch (e) {}
  // … draw from the chat state (null: no state yet)
}
W.onEvent('chatDataChanged', render);
render();
```

#### Static and shared widgets

| Property | Static widget | Shared widget |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Created by | `sendWidget` without `is_shared` | the first `sendWidget` (or inline send) with `is_shared` |
| Code, size, request flag | in the message | in the shared widget, the same in every message that shows it |
| Shared state (`public_data`) | in the message. A forward gets a copy as of the moment of forwarding, and a change reaches only the original | in the shared widget: one shared state for every message and forward, changed for all of them at once |
| Chat state (`chat_data`) | per message | per message, set at each send |
| Shown again elsewhere | by forwarding (a frozen copy) | by forwarding, or with [sendSharedWidget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendsharedwidget) / an [inline result](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#inline-mode-widgets) by its identifier |
| Requests from forwards | never | on a tap, if it was sent with `allow_queries`. They arrive as [shared\_widget\_query](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sharedwidgetquery) |
| Identifier | none | `widget.id` in every message that shows it, for everyone including the bot, and `widget_id` in the methods and updates |

A shared widget is like a poll: one object that any number of messages refer to. There is no separate method to create one: **the first send creates it.** To get its identifier in advance, to send the widget to many chats or to offer it in inline mode, send it once with `is_shared` to any chat (for example your own chat with the bot) and read `widget.id` from the returned message.

* **One widget, one behavior.** Every message showing a shared widget has the same HTML, size and request flag, as one poll cannot be anonymous in one message and public in another. Only the chat state belongs to each message.
* **Permanent.** A shared widget outlives every message that shows it: its shared state stays, [editSharedWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editsharedwidgetdata) edits it by its identifier after every carrier is deleted, and requests from live forwards keep arriving.
* **Immutable code.** For a new layout, send a new widget with `sendWidget`, which makes a new shared widget. Messages that show the old one keep it.

| Send | Use case | Shared state | Forwards may ask the bot | Change the shared state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sendWidget` | a widget with state | in the message, forwards get a copy | No | by the original's coordinates, only the original changes |
| `sendWidget` + `is_shared` | a ticker | a new shared widget | No, forwards follow it | by `widget_id` or by any original's coordinates |
| `sendWidget` + `is_shared` + `allow_queries` | live forwards (a poll) | a new shared widget | Yes, on a tap | by `widget_id` or by any original's coordinates |
| `sendSharedWidget` | send an existing shared widget again | the shared widget's, unchanged by the send | per the shared widget's flag | by `widget_id` or by any original's coordinates |

**Freshness.** An edit of a shared widget is visible at once to every read: opening the chat or scrolling to the message gives the current shared state. A widget already on screen gets a new shared state only if it asks for it with `TelegramWidget.watchPublicData()`. While at least one widget that called it is on screen, the app polls that shared widget (one poll per shared widget, whatever the number of messages showing it) at the shared widget's refresh period, and every widget on screen showing it gets `publicDataChanged`. A widget that does not watch gets its shared state only with the message. `unwatchPublicData()` stops asking. Both are synchronous, need no tap, can be called at any time and may be repeated. On a static widget they do nothing (its shared state, like every chat state, is pushed anyway), and a preview never watches.

The refresh period is a property of the shared widget: 30 seconds when created, changed only with `cache_time` in [editSharedWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editsharedwidgetdata) (5-3600 seconds: less than 5 is refused, more than 3600 is clamped). Choose it for how often the shared state changes: about 10 seconds for a price, minutes or an hour for something that changes slowly.

**Keep the newest state.** A poll can bring a shared state older than one the widget already drew from a request's answer or an earlier poll, and counts would jump back and forth. Put a revision in the shared state (`"r": 41`, raised on every edit, and in the answer too) and have the widget ignore anything older than the newest it has seen.

#### Widgets in groups

Bots can send widgets to basic groups and supergroups they are members of, forum topics included ([test server only](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#availability)). The bot needs the right to send other messages (`can_send_other_messages` in [ChatPermissions](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#chatpermissions): animations, games, stickers and inline bots). Widgets are checked like messages sent via an inline bot, so a group that does not give the bot this right refuses the widget too. Channels refuse widgets, sent directly or via the bot.

In a group:

* **The chat state is shared by all members.** Everyone sees the same chat state. Draw it per user with `TelegramWidget.viewer.id` (chess for two is one widget and one chat state).
* **Requests run on a tap only**, never in the background.
* **The bot addresses the message as usual**: the `chat` and `message_id` of a [widget\_query](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquery) are the ones it uses for its other messages in that group, and [editMessageWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editmessagewidgetdata) takes the same pair.

#### Inline mode widgets

A bot with inline mode enabled can return widgets as inline results ([test server only](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#availability)): an [InlineQueryResultArticle](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#inlinequeryresultarticle) whose `input_message_content` is a widget, in [answerInlineQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#answerinlinequery). A widget result cannot be sent in a channel. The content has the same two forms as sending:

* [InputWidgetMessageContent](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#inputwidgetmessagecontent): a new widget, with the fields of `sendWidget` (`html`, `width`, `height`, `public_data`, `chat_data`, the caption, `allow_queries`, `is_shared`). The server checks the code and the state when it saves the results (same limits, same errors). **Each send** of a result with `is_shared` creates **its own new shared widget**.
* [InputSharedWidgetMessageContent](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#inputsharedwidgetmessagecontent): an existing shared widget, by `widget_id`, with this message's `chat_data` and caption. Every send shows that shared widget.

```
POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/answerInlineQuery
{
  "inline_query_id": "<inline_query_id>",
  "results": [{
    "type": "article",
    "id": "ton",
    "title": "TON price",
    "description": "A live quote",
    "input_message_content": { "widget_id": "7770011223344556677", "caption": "TON price" }
  }]
}
```

* **The list of results shows the widget itself**, running as a [preview](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#previews) with the result's state (for a shared widget, its code and shared state): it takes no taps (a tap selects the result) and knows nothing about the user.
* **Every send becomes its own message** via the bot, with its own chat state.
* **Requests from a message sent via the bot run on a tap only.** The bot gets them as a [widget\_query](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquery) with `inline_message_id` instead of `chat` and `message_id`, together with the `chat_instance` and `chat_type` of the chat where the user tapped, and changes the message's state with [editMessageWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editmessagewidgetdata) and that `inline_message_id`.
* Only apps that support widgets receive widget results.

> **Note:** A bot does not receive the messages users send via it. To show one live shared state through inline mode, create the shared widget once with `sendWidget` and offer results by its identifier. A result with `html` and `is_shared` makes a new shared widget per send, and the bot sees its identifier only in a later request.

#### Requests to the bot

A request is a callback button inside the widget. The widget calls `TelegramWidget.request(data)` with 1-64 bytes of data. The bot receives a [widget\_query](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquery) update (or a [shared\_widget\_query](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sharedwidgetquery) from a forward) with who tapped, the request's data and the context. It answers with [answerWidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#answerwidgetquery) and optional `data` of up to 1024 bytes, which only the widget that asked receives, as its `result`.

**In the widget:**

```
button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  TelegramWidget.request('vote:2').then(
    (answer) => show(answer.result),   // { result: string | null }
    (error) => showError(error.code),  // error.name === 'WidgetRequestError'
  );
});
```

* **One tap, one call.** A request on a tap must be made in the tap's handler, synchronously, on the visible widget, and not from a timer, a promise callback or a later frame. One tap unlocks one call, shared with `openLink`, `openTelegramLink` and `copyText`.
* **One at a time.** A second call while a request waits for its answer rejects with `BUSY`.
* The promise resolves with `{ result }`: the bot's `data`, or `null` if it answered without any. It rejects with a [WidgetRequestError](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#widgetrequesterror) whose `code` says why: `NOT_ALLOWED`, `BUSY`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `TIMEOUT`, `FAILED`, `INVALID_ANSWER`.

**Where a widget may ask** is decided by the server for each message, from the widget's flags (a static widget's message, or the shared widget), and passed to the widget by the app:

| Message | On a tap | In the background | `viewer` | `chatType` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the original in the private chat with the bot | Yes | Yes | the user | `'private'` |
| an original in a group | Yes | No | the user | `'group'`, `'supergroup'` |
| an original sent via the bot | Yes | No | the user | the chat's type |
| a forward of a shared widget | Yes | No | the user | `null` |
| a forward of a static widget | No | No | `null` | `null` |

This is for a widget sent with `allow_queries`. A widget without it asks nowhere, its originals included, and has no `viewer`. Elsewhere `request()` rejects with `NOT_ALLOWED`.

**Background requests.** Only the original in the private chat with the bot may ask without a tap, and only while it is visible: one request when the widget appears on screen (scrolled into view, the app back in front), then at most one every 5 seconds while it stays visible. Apps create a widget before they show it, so a request the script makes in its first lines waits and goes out as soon as the widget appears. Ask for fresh state right at the start. Use background requests to refresh what this user sees while the chat is open. For what is the same for everyone, a [shared widget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#static-and-shared-widgets)'s shared state needs no requests at all. Neither the server nor the bot can tell a background request from a tap.

**In the bot.** A request from an original arrives in the field `widget_query` of [Update](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update), and one from a forwarded copy of a shared widget in the field `shared_widget_query`. If you pass `allowed_updates`, include both. Their fields depend on where the user tapped:

| Field | Original (private chat or group) | Original sent via the bot | Forward of a shared widget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| update | `widget_query` | `widget_query` | `shared_widget_query` |
| `id`, `from`, `data` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `chat`, `message_id` | Yes | No | No |
| `inline_message_id` | No | Yes | No |
| `chat_instance` | Yes | Yes, the chat of the tap | No |
| `chat_type` | No, see `chat.type` | Yes, the chat of the tap | No |
| `widget_id` | for a shared widget | for a shared widget | always |

```
{
  "update_id": 100000001,
  "widget_query": {
    "id": "8123456789012345678",
    "from": { "id": 111111111, "is_bot": false, "first_name": "Alice", "language_code": "en" },
    "chat": { "id": 111111111, "type": "private", "first_name": "Alice" },
    "message_id": 4242,
    "chat_instance": "901234567890123456",
    "widget_id": "7770011223344556677",
    "data": "refresh"

The query does not carry the widget's state: keep the authoritative state on your side, keyed by the message (or by `widget_id`), and check every request against it.

**Answering.** Call [answerWidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#answerwidgetquery) for **every** query, with or without `data`, within 15 seconds. Otherwise the widget's promise rejects with `TIMEOUT`. `data` is the only thing an answer carries: no change of state, no notification, no alert, no URL. The app shows nothing for an answer, and the widget shows the result itself.

```
POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/answerWidgetQuery
{ "widget_query_id": "8123456789012345678", "data": "{\"p\":5.47}" }
```

* **The answer does not change the state.** To change the chat state or the shared state, call the [methods that change it](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#changing-the-state), before or after answering. The widget gets `chatDataChanged` / `publicDataChanged` when the new state arrives, which can be before or after the answer. A widget that needs the new state at once (the user's own vote, the new board) gets it from the bot in the answer.
* **Answer also when something failed**, with a short text the widget can show: an unanswered request ends in the widget as `TIMEOUT`.
* **`from` and `widget_id` cannot be forged.** `from` is the user who tapped, authenticated by Telegram: no signature to check. `widget_id` is computed by the server from the tapped message, so a request cannot claim to come from another of your shared widgets. A forward's request carries nothing else about its place, so key “one vote per user” and paid actions on the pair **(`widget_id`, `from.id`)**.
* **Treat `data` as untrusted input**, like `callback_data`: check it against the state you keep.
* Do slow work after answering, then change the state.

На **10 ноября 2026** последняя версия — **Bot API 10.4**, выпущенная **9 ноября**. Главная новинка — **HTML-виджеты прямо внутри сообщений**, с CSS и JavaScript. В рабочем Telegram виджеты пока доступны **только в личном чате с ботом**, пересылка отключена. Внешних сетевых запросов у виджета нет; лимит HTML — 32 КБ и 4 КБ после сжатия. Отдельный сайт не нужен. [Документация](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets). В **aiogram 3.31.0** пока поддерживается Bot API 10.3, поэтому `sendWidget` вызовем через собственный `TelegramMethod`. Пример отправляет карточку с кнопкой копирования промокода. [Changelog aiogram](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/latest/changelog.html). Установите `python -m pip install aiogram==3.31.0`, задайте переменную окружения `BOT_TOKEN`: ```python import asyncio import os from aiogram import Bot, Dispatcher, F from aiogram.filters import Command from aiogram.methods.base import TelegramMethod from aiogram.types import Message class SendWidget(TelegramMethod[Message]): __returning__ = Message __api_method__ = "sendWidget" chat_id: int html: str caption: str | None = None HTML = """

Скидка 10%

Ваш промокод: HELLO10

""" dp = Dispatcher() @dp.message(Command("widget"), F.chat.type == "private") async def show_widget(message: Message, bot: Bot): await bot(SendWidget( chat_id=message.chat.id, html=HTML, caption="Скидка 10%. Промокод: HELLO10", )) async def main(): bot = Bot(token=os.environ["BOT_TOKEN"]) await dp.start_polling(bot) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ``` Отправьте боту `/widget` в клиенте Telegram с поддержкой виджетов. Кнопка выполнит JavaScript внутри карточки и скопирует код; `caption` послужит текстом для уведомлений и старых клиентов. [Метод `sendWidget`](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendwidget).
